item.title: Multi-Paradigm Collaborative Adversarial Attack Against Multi-Modal Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes MPCAttack, a Multi-Paradigm Collaborative Attack for multi-modal LLMs (MLLMs).
  • Uses aggregated semantic representations from both images and texts to jointly optimize adversarial perturbations via a Multi-Paradigm Collaborative Optimisation (MPCO) strategy.
  • Employs contrastive matching across multi-paradigm features to improve transferability and mitigate representation bias.
  • Evaluates on multiple benchmarks, reporting stronger performance than prior methods for both targeted and untargeted attacks against open- and closed-source MLLMs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yuanbo Li', 'Tianyang Xu', 'Cong Hu', 'Tao Zhou', 'Xiao-Jun Wu', 'Josef Kittler']
  • Tags: ['Adversarial Attacks', 'Multi-Modal LLMs', 'Transferability', 'Evasion']

item.title: Towards Highly Transferable Vision-Language Attack via Semantic-Augmented Dynamic Contrastive Interaction
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SADCA, a semantic-augmented dynamic contrastive adversarial attack targeting vision-language (VLP) models.
  • Uses progressive perturbation with dynamic cross-modal interactions (adversarial images with text) to disrupt image-text alignment.
  • Introduces a contrastive mechanism with adversarial/positive/negative samples to enforce semantic inconsistency and improve transferability.
  • Reports improved transfer-based attack performance across datasets and models; notes common input transformations further enhance attack effectiveness.

  • Research

item.title: When Safety Collides: Resolving Multi-Category Harmful Conflicts in Text-to-Image Diffusion via Adaptive Safety Guidance
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Conflict-aware Adaptive Safety Guidance (CASG) for text-to-image diffusion models to reduce harmful content generation.
  • Introduces CaCI to identify the most relevant harmful category based on the model’s evolving state, and CrGA to apply safety guidance aligned to that category only.
  • Aims to prevent “harmful conflicts” where mitigating one harmful category can amplify others.
  • Reports improved results on T2I safety benchmarks (up to 15.4% reduction in harmful rate).

Paper Type

  • Research

  • Authors: ['Yongli Xiang', 'Ziming Hong', 'Zhaoqing Wang', 'Xiangyu Zhao', 'Bo Han', 'Tongliang Liu']

item.title: TTP: Test-Time Padding for Adversarial Detection and Robust Adaptation on Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Test-Time Padding (TTP), a lightweight test-time defense for vision-language models (e.g., CLIP).
  • Uses embedding changes (cosine similarity shift) after spatial padding to detect adversarial inputs with a universal threshold.
  • For detected adversarial samples, applies trainable padding and a similarity-aware ensemble to restore attention patterns and improve final predictions.
  • Reports improved adversarial robustness and maintains clean accuracy across multiple CLIP backbones and fine-grained benchmarks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zhiwei Li', 'Yitian Pang', 'Weining Wang', 'Zhenan Sun', 'Qi Li']
  • Tags: ['adversarial detection', 'test-time defenses', 'vision-language models', 'robustness/robust adaptation']

item.title: DisPatch: Disarming Adversarial Patches in Object Detection with Diffusion Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes DisPatch, a diffusion-model-based defense for object detection against adversarial patch attacks.
  • Uses a 'regenerate and rectify' pipeline: regenerates the image with diffusion models to align it with benign data, then replaces suspected adversarial regions with regenerated benign counterparts.
  • Claims attack-agnostic operation (no prior knowledge of patch type) and effectiveness against both hiding and creating (false object) attacks.
  • Reports improved detection performance (mAP) and reduced attack success rate, with robustness against adaptive attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jin Ma', 'Mohammed Aldeen', 'Christopher Salas', 'Feng Luo', 'Mashrur Chowdhury', "Mert Pes\\'e", 'Long Cheng']
  • Tags: ['adversarial patches', 'diffusion-model defense', 'object detection security', 'attack-agnostic defense']

item.title: IAG: Input-aware Backdoor Attack on VLM-based Visual Grounding
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes IAG, a multi-target, input-aware backdoor attack against VLM-based visual grounding systems.
  • Uses a text-conditioned UNet to generate imperceptible, target-semantics triggers conditioned on arbitrary object descriptions.
  • Trains with objectives balancing language capability and perceptual reconstruction to maintain stealth and preserve benign grounding performance.
  • Evaluates across multiple VLMs and visual grounding benchmarks, reporting high attack success rates with robustness against existing defenses and transferability across models/datasets.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: DifAttack++: Query-Efficient Black-Box Adversarial Attack via Hierarchical Disentangled Feature Space in Cross-Domain
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes DifAttack++ for efficient black-box score-based adversarial attacks.
  • Introduces a hierarchical disentangled feature approach separating an Adversarial Feature (AF) from a Visual Feature (VF) to optimize only AF during black-box querying.
  • Uses cross-domain training with clean images and surrogate-model adversarial examples to enable query-efficient transfer/generalization.
  • Claims higher attack success rate, better query efficiency, and improved visual quality of adversarial examples.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: OmniPatch: A Universal Adversarial Patch for ViT-CNN Cross-Architecture Transfer in Semantic Segmentation
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces OmniPatch, a universal adversarial patch for semantic segmentation that transfers across different input images and across both ViT and CNN architectures.
  • Targets black-box scenarios where adversary does not know target model weights, focusing on practical attack transferability.
  • Claims to improve over prior methods that are either image-wide perturbations or patches optimized for a single architecture, limiting real-world applicability.

item.title: Visual Exclusivity Attacks: Automatic Multimodal Red Teaming via Agentic Planning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Visual Exclusivity (VE) attacks where harmful outcomes rely on reasoning over visual content (e.g., technical schematics) rather than brittle image payload tricks.
  • Introduces MM-Plan, an agentic, multi-turn planning framework that optimizes attacker strategy synthesis (via GRPO) for multimodal jailbreaking beyond reactive turn-by-turn prompting.
  • Presents VE-Safety, a dataset for benchmarking reasoning-dependent multimodal visual threats using human curation.
  • Reports substantially higher attack success rates than prior multimodal red teaming baselines against frontier models.

item.title: Principled Steering via Null-space Projection for Jailbreak Defense in Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes NullSteer, a null-space projection-based activation steering method for defending vision-language models against visual jailbreak attacks.
  • Constructs refusal directions that produce zero perturbation in a benign subspace while projecting changes onto potentially harmful activation directions.
  • Claims improved theoretical interpretability/robustness compared to prior activation steering approaches that may cause over-refusal.
  • Reports experimental results showing reduced harmful outputs (ASR reductions) while maintaining comparable performance on general benchmarks.

item.title: DTVI: Dual-Stage Textual and Visual Intervention for Safe Text-to-Image Generation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes DTVI, a dual-stage inference-time defense for safe text-to-image diffusion generation.
  • Uses category-aware, sequence-level intervention in the full prompt embedding to address malicious semantics beyond token-level methods.
  • Adds a second stage during visual generation to further attenuate remaining unsafe influences.
  • Evaluates on unsafe/adversarial prompts across multiple harmful categories, reporting high defense success rates with preserved benign quality.

Paper Type

  • Research

  • Authors: ['Binhong Tan', 'Zhaoxin Wang', 'Handing Wang']
  • Tags: ['Text-to-Image Safety', 'Inference-Time Defense', 'Adversarial Prompt Defense', 'Diffusion Models', 'Content Moderation']

item.title: Thermal Topology Collapse: Universal Physical Patch Attacks on Infrared Vision Systems
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes UPPA, a universal physical adversarial patch attack tailored to infrared vision systems.
  • Uses parametrized Bezier-block perturbation modeling with PSO to optimize across the global data distribution for robustness under physical deformations.
  • Materializes digital perturbations into real cold patches that induce smooth low-temperature changes consistent with IR sensor physics.
  • Reports high physical attack success with no online computation, plus strong cross-domain generalization and black-box transferability.

item.title: Adversarial Camouflage
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes “Adversarial Camouflage,” a physical-world privacy protection method that uses optimized low-dimensional patterns applied to faces.
  • Generates perturbations to maximize recognition error across multiple face recognition architectures, including black-box transfer settings.
  • Evaluates performance degradation in simulations and reports real-world human experiments, including analysis of cross-model robustness and transferability.

item.title: JANUS: A Lightweight Framework for Jailbreaking Text-to-Image Models via Distribution Optimization
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes JANUS, a lightweight framework to jailbreak text-to-image (T2I) models by optimizing a structured distribution over prompts.
  • Uses a low-dimensional mixing policy over two semantically anchored prompt distributions with black-box, end-to-end reward signals from the T2I system and its safety filters.
  • Evaluates on open-source and commercial T2I models and reports improved attack success rates (ASR-8) while maintaining semantic similarity (CLIP scores).
  • Findings suggest vulnerabilities/structural weaknesses in existing T2I safety pipelines and call for distribution-aware defenses.

Paper Type

item.title: When Minor Edits Matter: LLM-Driven Prompt Attack for Medical VLM Robustness in Ultrasound
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an adversarial evaluation framework that uses an LLM to generate minimally edited, clinically plausible prompt variants to attack medical VLMs.
  • Evaluates multiple SOTA Med-VLMs on ultrasound multiple-choice question answering benchmarks under these prompt-edit attacks.
  • Studies how attacker LLM capability and model confidence relate to attack success and identifies consistent vulnerability patterns across models.

item.title: Inverting Neural Networks: New Methods to Generate Neural Network Inputs from Prescribed Outputs
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies neural network inversion to construct input images that achieve prescribed output classes/scores.
  • Proposes two inversion techniques: Jacobian-based root-finding (forward-pass) and layer-wise iterative inversion with null-space randomization (backward-pass).
  • Shows that generated inputs can look random-like while producing near-perfect classification outputs, indicating exploitable weaknesses.

item.title: VGS-Decoding: Visual Grounding Score Guided Decoding for Hallucination Mitigation in Medical VLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes VGS-Decoding, a training-free decoding-time method to mitigate hallucinations in medical vision-language models by using a per-token Visual Grounding Score (VGS).
  • VGS estimates each token’s reliance on visual evidence by comparing token probability distributions under original vs. distorted images, enabling adaptive reweighting during generation.
  • Reports improvements on MIMIC-Diff-VQA and VQA-RAD across multiple medical VLMs, with limited inference overhead and no extra training.

item.title: Conflict-Aware Fusion: Mitigating Logic Inertia in Large Language Models via Structured Cognitive Priors
item.description:
Summary

  • Evaluates LLM reasoning reliability using stress tests involving structured rule perturbations (rule deletion, contradictory evidence injection, logic-preserving rewrites, multi-law equivalence stacking).
  • Identifies a failure mode called “Logic Inertia” where models override facts under contradictions (noted as dropping to 0.0000 accuracy).
  • Proposes “Conflict-Aware Fusion,” a defense-like architecture separating premise verification from logical deduction to mitigate contradiction failures and improve robustness to missing evidence.
  • Includes controlled evaluation framework and reports improved accuracy on both base and contradictory tests, with related tooling/repro links.

Paper Type

  • Research Paper

Additional Information

  • Tags: ['LLM security', 'Robust reasoning', 'Adversarial evaluation', 'Defense/mitigation architecture']

item.title: A Training-free Method for LLM Text Attribution
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a training-free, zero-shot statistical testing framework to attribute LLM-generated text to specific model sets (in-house vs non-sanctioned) while guaranteeing low false positives.
  • Models LLM text generation as a history-dependent stochastic process and provides theoretical exponential decay bounds on Type I/Type II errors with text length.
  • Extends guarantees from white-box access to black-box sampling, including sample-size requirements, and provides matching information-theoretic lower bounds.
  • Includes experiments and evaluates robustness under adversarial post-editing.

item.title: Seamless Deception: Larger Language Models Are Better Knowledge Concealers
item.description:
Summary

  • Trains classifiers to detect whether LLMs are concealing harmful knowledge during audits, leveraging deception-detection patterns.
  • Finds that detection is more reliable on smaller models than with human evaluators, and that gradient-based concealment traces are easier to identify than prompt-based ones.
  • Shows poor generalization across unseen model architectures/topics, and that concealment traces fade as model scale increases, yielding near-random detection beyond 70B parameters.
  • Argues that black-box-only auditing is limited and calls for more robust methods to detect active knowledge hiding.

Paper Type

  • Research

  • Tags: ['deception-detection', 'LLM auditing', 'black-box evaluation', 'knowledge concealment']

item.title: FACTUM: Mechanistic Detection of Citation Hallucination in Long-Form RAG
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes FACTUM, a mechanistic detection framework for citation hallucinations in long-form Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
  • Introduces four mechanistic scores (CAS, BAS, PFS, PAS) that analyze internal model pathway behavior to distinguish correct vs unsupported citations.
  • Finds citation correctness correlates with higher Parametric Force (PFS) and attention-sink usage (BAS), and that detection signatures shift with model scale.

item.title: Hidden State Poisoning Attacks against Mamba-based Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes and studies Hidden State Poisoning Attacks (HiSPA) against Mamba/SSM-based language models, where short trigger phrases partially erase/overwrite hidden-state information.
  • Introduces a benchmark (RoBench-25) to evaluate information retrieval under HiSPAs and shows SSMs are vulnerable while pure Transformers are not.
  • Demonstrates the attack transfers to Mamba-2 and affects hybrid SSM-Transformer models (e.g., Jamba-1.7-Mini) and weakens performance on prompt-injection evaluation (Open-Prompt-Injections).
  • Includes interpretability analysis to identify hidden-layer patterns that may support a HiSPA mitigation system.

Paper Type

item.title: SafeSearch: Do Not Trade Safety for Utility in LLM Search Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Evaluates LLM search agents with red-teaming and finds they can be more harmful than base LLMs due to lowered refusal thresholds and document-assisted synthesis of unsafe content.
  • Shows that utility-oriented fine-tuning can intensify harmful behavior in these agents.
  • Proposes SafeSearch, a multi-objective RL method that improves safety via final-output rewards plus query-level shaping to penalize unsafe queries.
  • Reports strong empirical results: >90% reduction in harmfulness across multiple red-teaming datasets with minimal QA performance loss.

Paper Type

item.title: Prompt-Induced Linguistic Fingerprints for LLM-Generated Fake News Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a fake-news detection method for LLM-generated content using “prompt-induced linguistic fingerprints.”
  • Uses distributional divergence and word-level probability reconstruction to detect statistical traces caused by malicious prompting.
  • Introduces LIFE and enhances it with key-fragment techniques to amplify subtle linguistic differences.
  • Reports state-of-the-art detection performance on LLM-generated fake news and robustness on human-written fake news.

item.title: SafeConstellations: Mitigating Over-Refusals in LLMs Through Task-Aware Representation Steering
item.description:
Summary

  • Addresses LLM “over-refusal” (benign instructions incorrectly rejected due to safety mechanisms).
  • Provides a mechanistic analysis of task-dependent embedding trajectory patterns that correlate with refusal vs non-refusal behavior.
  • Introduces SafeConstellations, an inference-time representation/trajectory steering method to guide outputs toward non-refusal for tasks prone to over-refusal.

item.title: SecureBreak -- A dataset towards safe and secure models
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces SecureBreak, a manually annotated dataset for detecting harmful/unsafe LLM outputs.
  • Targets vulnerabilities in security alignment by covering multiple risk categories linked to residual unsafe generations (e.g., jailbreaking/prompt-injection outcomes).
  • Evaluates usefulness for post-generation safety filtering and for fine-tuning to improve detection robustness across risk types.

item.title: Epistemic Observability in Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Finds language models’ self-reported confidence is inversely correlated with accuracy, suggesting they are most confident when fabricating.
  • Proves impossibility results: with only text output observation, no monitoring/learning algorithm can reliably distinguish honest vs fabricated responses under ambiguous world states.
  • Introduces an “entropy/log-probability tensor interface” that exposes computational byproducts (e.g., per-token entropy) to enable reliable detection of fabrications.
  • Provides a cost surface/lookup map linking verification budget allocation to detection accuracy across judge strategies.

item.title: Cross-Context Verification: Hierarchical Detection of Benchmark Contamination through Session-Isolated Analysis
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Cross-Context Verification (CCV), a black-box method for detecting benchmark contamination/leakage by solving the same problem across N independent, session-isolated runs and measuring solution diversity.
  • Introduces Hierarchical Cross-Context Architecture (HCCA), a multi-agent framework that restricts information across analytical roles to reduce confirmation bias during contamination detection.
  • Evaluates on 9 SWE-bench Verified problems (45 trials, Claude Opus 4.6) and reports strong separation between contaminated vs genuine reasoning.
  • Finds that repeating verification can increase false positives and suggests that information restriction—not additional verification stages—drives effectiveness.

Paper Type

  • Research

  • Tags: ['benchmark-contamination detection', 'black-box evaluation', 'LLM red teaming', 'information restriction']

item.title: Alignment Whack-a-Mole : Finetuning Activates Verbatim Recall of Copyrighted Books in Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows that finetuning can bypass alignment/safety protections and trigger high-rate verbatim recall of copyrighted books from held-out data.
  • Demonstrates extraction of long verbatim spans (up to 460+ words) using only semantic prompts, and significant generalization across unrelated authors.
  • Findings indicate latent memorization in pretrained weights that is reactivated by author-specific finetuning, affecting multiple frontier LLM providers similarly.

item.title: The Hidden Puppet Master: A Theoretical and Real-World Account of Emotional Manipulation in LLMs

item.title: PAVE: Premise-Aware Validation and Editing for Retrieval-Augmented LLMs

Summary

  • Proposes PAVE, an inference-time validation/editing layer for retrieval-augmented LLMs.
  • Decomposes retrieved context into question-conditioned atomic premises, drafts an answer, scores premise support, and revises low-support outputs.
  • Emphasizes auditable traces (premises, support scores, revision decisions) to reduce unwarranted commitment despite retrieval evidence.
  • Evaluated via ablations on evidence-grounded QA benchmarks, showing improved accuracy over post-retrieval baselines.

item.title: FinReflectKG -- HalluBench: GraphRAG Hallucination Benchmark for Financial Question Answering Systems
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces HalluBench/FinBench-QA-Hallucination to benchmark hallucination detection in KG-augmented financial QA over SEC 10-K filings.
  • Creates groundedness-labeled examples using evidence-linkage requiring both supporting text chunks and extracted relational triplets.
  • Evaluates multiple hallucination detection methods (LLM judges, classifiers, NLI, span detectors, embedding-based) under clean vs noisy/no KG-triplet conditions.
  • Finds substantial performance degradation for many methods when noisy KG triplets are introduced; embedding methods are comparatively more robust.

item.title: RedacBench: Can AI Erase Your Secrets?
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces RedacBench, a benchmark to evaluate policy-conditioned redaction by LMs.
  • Assesses security effectiveness (removing sensitive/sensitive propositions) and utility (preserving non-sensitive semantics).
  • Uses human-authored texts across individual/corporate/government domains paired with security policies.
  • Provides annotated propositions and evaluates multiple redaction strategies and models, enabling systematic security/robustness evaluation.

item.title: Enhancing Safety of Large Language Models via Embedding Space Separation
item.description:
